# The smallest field generated by a power over the maximal abelian extension

<a id="statement"></a>
## A power that preserves measure and minimum relation length

Let \(\alpha\) be a nontorsion algebraic unit, \(p_\alpha\) its monic minimal polynomial over \(\mathbb Q\), and \(F=\mathbb Q^{\rm ab}\) the maximal abelian extension of \(\mathbb Q\).
Write \(m(\alpha)=[\mathbb Q(\alpha):\mathbb Q]h(\alpha)\) for logarithmic Mahler measure and \(\lambda(\alpha)\) for the least sum of absolute coefficients of a nonzero integer polynomial vanishing at \(\alpha\).
Let \(g\) be the gcd of the positive exponents with nonzero coefficient in \(p_\alpha\), and put \(\beta=\alpha^g\).
Then
\[
  p_\alpha(X)=p_\beta(X^g),\qquad
  m(\alpha)=m(\beta),\qquad \lambda(\alpha)=\lambda(\beta),\qquad
  F(\beta)=\bigcap_{n\ge1}F(\alpha^n).
  \tag{1}
\]
In particular \(\delta=[F(\beta):F]\) is the minimum of \([F(\alpha^n):F]\) over all positive integers \(n\).
The minimum is attained at \(g\) and every positive multiple of \(g\).

For fixed \(B>0\) and integer \(D\ge1\), the units satisfying
\[
         m(\alpha)\le B,\qquad [F(\alpha^n):F]\le D
                     \quad\hbox{for some } n\ge1
         \tag{2}
\]
have their minimal polynomials in finitely many families.
Each family consists of all the irreducible polynomials \(f(X^s)\), \(s\ge1\), for a single monic unit polynomial \(f\) irreducible over \(\mathbb Q\) whose positive support exponents have gcd one.
Both \(m\) and \(\lambda\) are constant in each family.
This includes arbitrary radicals of units of bounded absolute degree, as well as arbitrarily varying units whose selected power has bounded degree only over \(F\).

<a id="fields"></a>
## The intersection of the fields

Writing \(p_\alpha(X)=f(X^g)\) gives an irreducible monic \(f\), because a proper factorization of \(f\) would give one of \(p_\alpha\).
Since \(f(\beta)=0\), we have \(f=p_\beta\), and \([\mathbb Q(\alpha):\mathbb Q(\beta)]=g\).
The degree identity and \(h(\alpha^g)=g h(\alpha)\) give equality of the measures.
Substitution of \(X^g\) into a relation at \(\beta\) gives \(\lambda(\alpha)\le\lambda(\beta)\).
In the other direction, partition any nonzero integer relation at \(\alpha\) by its exponents modulo \(g\), writing its polynomial as \(\sum_{j=0}^{g-1}X^jH_j(X^g)\).
The elements \(1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{g-1}\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\), so every \(H_j(\beta)\) vanishes.
At least one \(H_j\) is a nonzero polynomial, and its length is at most that of the given relation.

Fix \(n\ge1\) and put \(L=F(\alpha^n)\) and \(r=[L(\alpha):L]\).
The field \(L\) contains all roots of unity, so \(L(\alpha)\) splits the separable polynomial \(X^n-\alpha^n\) over \(L\).
The map \(\sigma\mapsto\sigma(\alpha)/\alpha\) embeds its Galois group into the \(n\)-th roots of unity since the latter are fixed by every \(\sigma\).
Its image has order \(r\), and every image element has \(r\)-th power one.
It follows that \(\gamma=\alpha^r\) belongs to \(L\).
Extension of scalars to \(L\) from \(\mathbb Q(\gamma)\), and the polynomial \(X^r-\gamma\), give
\[
     r=[L(\alpha):L]\le [\mathbb Q(\alpha):\mathbb Q(\gamma)]\le r .
\]
Consequently the monic polynomial \(p_\gamma(X^r)\), which vanishes at \(\alpha\), has precisely the degree of \(p_\alpha\) and equals it.
Every positive support exponent of \(p_\alpha\) is therefore divisible by \(r\), giving \(r\mid g\) and \(\beta=\gamma^{g/r}\in L\).
This proves \(F(\beta)\subseteq F(\alpha^n)\) for every \(n\); taking \(n=g\) gives the intersection identity.
If \(g\mid n\), the reverse inclusion follows from \(\alpha^n=\beta^{n/g}\).

<a id="finite"></a>
## The finite families and the degree bound

The [relative height bound of Amoroso and Delsinne](../audits/literature/AD07/Yin_U001.md#rational-base) gives an absolute \(c>0\) such that \(h(\beta)\ge c/H(\delta)\), where
\[
             H(t)=\frac{t(\log(2t))^4}{(\log\log(5t))^3}\qquad(t\ge1).
\]
The rational-base statement applies to \(F\) and to the nontorsion \(\beta\).
Using (1) gives
\[
 \deg p_\beta\le c^{-1}m(\alpha)H(\delta),\qquad
 \log\lambda(\alpha)
       \le m(\alpha)\bigl(1+c^{-1}(\log 2)H(\delta)\bigr).
 \tag{3}
\]
For the second bound, the coefficient length of a monic polynomial of degree \(d\) and logarithmic measure \(m\) is at most \(2^d e^m\), by multiplying \(1+|z|\le2\max(1,|z|)\) over its roots.
Under (2), \(\delta\le D\), so (3) bounds \(\deg p_\beta\) in terms of \(B,D\).
The same coefficient estimate bounds every coefficient of \(p_\beta\); hence only finitely many such polynomials occur.

Take the finite list of all monic irreducible nontorsion unit polynomials \(f\) whose positive support exponents have gcd one, whose measure is at most \(B\), and for whose root \(b\) one has \([F(b):F]\le D\).
The relative degree is independent of the root since \(F/\mathbb Q\) is normal.
Each \(\alpha\) satisfying (2) is obtained from this list by (1).
Conversely every irreducible \(f(X^s)\) from the list has the measure of \(f\), and its roots have \(s\)-th powers of relative degree at most \(D\).
The gcd of its positive support exponents is \(s\), so the list represents each minimal polynomial exactly once.
The [norm bound for radicals of bounded-degree seeds](Yin_C_G0206_v1.md#statement) excludes measures approaching zero for that smaller class; (1)–(3) identify the polynomials and the minimum relation lengths throughout each bounded range in (2).

In particular if \(m(\alpha_i)\) stays bounded and \(\lambda(\alpha_i)\to\infty\), then \(\min_{n\ge1}[F(\alpha_i^n):F]\to\infty\) by (3).
This also forces the absolute degrees of all positive powers to tend uniformly to infinity.
The [interval construction conditional on failure of the gap](Yin_C_G0345_v185.md#prescribed) would therefore escape every fixed relative degree bound even after arbitrary powering.
The formulas impose no bound on \(\delta\) for all units of bounded measure.

<a id="count"></a>
## Counts by degree

At degree \(d\) each polynomial \(f\) on the list contributes exactly one class if \(\deg f\mid d\) and \(f(X^{d/\deg f})\) is irreducible, and zero otherwise.
Thus (2) gives \(O_{B,D}(1)\) classes at each degree, \(O_{B,D}(N)\) through degree \(N\), and \(O_{B,D}(N^2)\) individual conjugates through degree \(N\).

The cumulative orders are attained when \(D=1\) and \(B=\log\phi\), where \(\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\).
For every \(s\ge1\) take the positive real \(a=\phi^{1/s}\) and put \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)\) and \(e=[K(a):K]\le s\).
The conjugates of \(a\) over \(K\) all have modulus \(a\), so the absolute value in this real embedding of the relative norm is \(a^e=\phi^{e/s}\).
It is a positive unit of \(K\), since the norm is a real unit and taking its absolute value changes at most its sign.
There is no positive unit \(u\) of \(K\) strictly between \(1\) and \(\phi\): according to its norm, its integral trace would be \(u+u^{-1}\in(2,3)\) or \(u-u^{-1}\in(0,1)\).
Hence \(e=s\).
Since \(a^s=\phi\) generates \(K\), the polynomial \(X^{2s}-X^s-1\) is the minimal polynomial of \(a\).
Its measure is \(\log\phi\), and \(a^s\in F\) since \(K/\mathbb Q\) is quadratic.
These classes at every even degree give \(\gg N\) classes and \(\gg N^2\) conjugates through degree \(N\).
